en: Lightning strikes the tallest objects, so you must seek shelter inside a fully enclosed building during a thunderstorm.
A typhoon's storm surge pushes seawater inland, so coastal residents must evacuate to higher ground to avoid drowning.
Stagnant floodwater left after a rainstorm breeds mosquitoes that carry dengue fever, so empty all standing water around your house.
Wearing an N95 mask during a volcanic ashfall prevents you from inhaling tiny rock particles that can damage your lungs.
The Moon's gravity creates high tides that can produce dangerous rip currents, so always swim near a lifeguard.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can permanently burn your retinas and cause blindness.
Washing your hands with soap after playing in soil kills hookworm larvae and prevents them from entering your body.
El Nino causes severe dry seasons in the Philippines, so communities must build rainwater catchers to store drinking water.
High humidity stops your sweat from evaporating quickly, which raises your body temperature and increases your risk of heatstroke.
Earth's ozone layer blocks the Sun's ultraviolet radiation, so applying sunscreen protects your skin from harmful sunburns.
A sudden drop in barometric pressure often signals an approaching typhoon, so fishermen should return to shore immediately.
Permeable rocks like sandstone allow rainwater to filter into underground aquifers, providing communities with clean drinking water.
